title: The Danger of Listening to Sophists
english: For they say that it is not possible to be in my flesh, because my soul has been played with by the mockeries of the present; for the flesh, flowing and lacking self-control, is very weak, and so he who commits fornication in the body sins (Ps 37:9b,10).

From the depth of repentance, bringing forth groans through repentance, not from superficiality or pretension like the hypocrites of repentance; therefore also, daring, he says: 'To you, Lord, as truly the desire of my heart is before you' (Ps 37:9b,10); for indeed all the vile impulse is far from you and is hidden from you, but the desire of my heart, desiring to pass from wickedness into genuine virtue, possesses a good desire, which one does not find in dreams. He may also speak concerning the vile desire: since the vile impulse lying within me has not eluded you, confessing concerning this I groan, as if the groan concerning it, being bold, would not be hidden from you; for it is praiseworthy to groan over evils (Ps 37:11–13).

Of my heart—that is, of my intellectual power—undergoing turmoil, my strength according to common understandings has abandoned me, but also the knowledge of the truths, the light of my eyes—that is, being the mind—is not with me; for having determined according to reason, I will not be able to conceive clearly or to think strongly. There may be strength in him saying this, and the light of his eyes is the right reason according to which it is rational. The right reason did not abandon him, and it no longer seems to be with him, the strength of the heart being called so according to the guidance of the practical [sciences], and the light of the eyes according to the illuminating by the clarity of those seeing.

And he lived, he says, loving friends and neighbors, having found these standing warily and as enemies, having rushed to turn away from evil and to do the good. But also they were previously near me in relationship and disposition, from afar enemies...

One should speak thus: if anyone falls by various circumstances, he is abandoned by all those who were previously near him, both friends and neighbors, just as he is also accused by the one he formerly loved. These images are found in Job. And those who, seeking my soul harmfully and through strife, came forward and wished to surround me with violence, thought they were leading me down with coercive words as if they were proofs; but they hurried to subject me to the investigation of evils, through which vanity spoke to me. For the argument was not as a proof, but as a vain and deceptive sophistry. And the vanity through which they sophistically argue all day long, that is, through life, they practice deceit, not bringing proofs to the things, but deciding to seize [the mind] sophistically.

He who judges to guard himself will be deafened, not receiving vain hearing toward the deceitful and deceptive words, not wishing to have their sense from hearing (Ps 37:14-15); and much more, he would not wish to answer or to refute such words, like a senseless person. For it is said in other places that it is foolish to refute very gentle words. 'I became, he says, toward such men as if not hearing and not having reproaches in my mouth.' For there is much danger in hearing defamatory words and in conversing about proposed problems [which lead to] punishment. Therefore, it is blessed to be deaf to such things and to be considered as if one were not refuting them.

Since, having despised all others, I hoped in you alone, O Lord, and You being God, will hear me; having prayed, I began, O Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger (Ps 37:16). For often those who associate with me, even if they sinned, bring the past deeds as insults, as if through this to hinder my repentance.
